title: Pixel 6 postmortem: How Google’s flawed reboot defined future hardware [Video]
snippet: I think there are few smartphones in the past decade that have arrived carrying the sheer weight of expectation that greeted the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro in late 2021. Now on life support, just what did we learn from 2021’s reboot for the brand? more…
fullText:
I think there are few smartphones in the past decade that have arrived carrying the sheer weight of expectation that greeted the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro in late 2021. Now on life support, just what did we learn from 2021’s reboot for the brand?

There was a lot of bubbling hype around ahead of Made by Google before the Pixel 6 was unveiled. I think a lot of that is due to just how flip-flop the Pixel lineup had become after years of identity crises, weird experimental gestures, compromised battery sizes, and following on from the charming but overtly mid-range Pixel 5, Google said enough was enough and finally decided to swing for the fences.

I think fans hoped that Google was done playing nice and coming second to Samsung and Apple. The Pixel 6 series was built to make a statement, introducing a brand new design language, custom silicon in the shape of Google Tensor, huge camera sensor upgrades, and a shockingly competitive price tag.

For more video content, subscribe to 9to5Google on YouTube.

	

Yet, looking back with years of hindsight, the Pixel 6 duo remains one of the most polarizing Google releases, probably ever, but we can’t get away from the important fact that it laid the technological foundation for everything Pixel represents today, but it did so while putting early adopters through a gauntlet of software bugs, sluggish biometrics, thermal throttling, and atrocious cellular connectivity.

So with that in mind, this is the Google Pixel 6 and 6 Pro: the good, the bad, the ugly, and how this turbulent reboot shaped the future of Pixel.

Before the Pixel 6, Google’s hardware design wasn’t exactly tearing up trees. I’d say it was best described as understated, if not entirely apologetic. The fabric cases notwithstanding, and maybe the soft-touch bio-resin finish of the Pixel 5 aside, nothing about them screamed “I am a flagship phone” across a crowded room.

I genuinely feel that the Pixel 6 changed that overnight, but without losing some of the “playful” feel that has been a hallmark of basically all Google hardware. 

Dominated by a bold, edge-to-edge camera visor across the rear, the design was, dare I say it, instantly iconic. Instead of an awkward off-center stove-top camera island that rocked incessantly when placed on a flat desk, the camera bar acted as a natural kickstand. It gave the Pixel line an unmistakable silhouette that Google continues to iterate on today.

One thing that was interesting at the time and even more so today is how the line was separated at launch. Two distinct yet similar designs with dual-tone pastel glass backs. The Pixel 6 had a bigger dash of “fun” with the Sorta Seafoam, Kinda Coral, and the striking Stormy Black. The 6 Pro leaned into more traditional executive styling with polished aluminum rails and curved front glass, whereas the standard Pixel 6 has that flat display glass, matte black borders, and a boxier aesthetic.

However, the hardware was not without ergonomic pain points. Both devices were heavy, slippery, and massive. Google completely abandoned the compact form factor of the Pixel 5, offering no refuge for small-phone purists after the palm-friendly 4a and even the smaller Pixel 4. The polished rails of the Pro were a magnet for grease, while the glossy back panels made both phones still feel like a wet soap bar without a protective case.

Complaints aside, the design was arguably the biggest standout. I think they still look great today.

Enter Google Tensor: It’s time to chip in

The biggest architectural gamble with the Pixel 6 generation was the departure from Qualcomm Snapdragon processors in favor of in-house silicon. Before launch, we’d heard so much about the first-generation Google Tensor chip thanks to numerous leaks, but really had no idea what it would bring to the table.

Developed in partnership with Samsung’s Foundry, Tensor, or “Tensor G1” as it is known today, was not designed to beat Apple’s A-series chips or Qualcomm’s Snapdragon lineup on synthetic Geekbench benchmarks. Google’s main pitch was on-device machine learning.

The first-gen Tensor chip unlocked voice typing through Google Assistant that was fast and accurate enough to genuinely replace keyboard tapping, real-time live translation, Magic Eraser photo cleanup, and instant offline speech transcription. These are now commonplace, but they felt like real differentiators at the time.

In everyday UI tasks, the Pixel 6 felt fluid and remarkably responsive. Paired with Android 12 and the debut of the Material You’s dynamic theming engine, using the phone felt fresh, cohesive, and modern but styled with Google’s trademark flourishes.

The trade-off was efficiency. Fabricated on Samsung’s 5nm LPE node, the first Tensor generation struggled, well, struggled is an understatement, with sustained thermal performance. Under heavy loads or prolonged 4K recording sessions, the phone warmed up rapidly. Gaming performance was volatile, and battery life was wildly inconsistent between individual units.

The complaints: Optical scanners and modem nightmares

I think it’s fair to say that those issues were the tip of the iceberg. The first six months of the Pixel 6’s lifecycle were marred by two notorious hardware bottlenecks: the optical fingerprint reader and the cellular modem.

Google made the controversial decision to ditch the ultra-reliable rear-mounted Pixel Imprint capacitive scanner in favor of an under-display optical sensor. You fell into a couple of camps with this problem in particular. I can’t say I had a single issue, save for unlocking being slower than the competition at the time, but for thousands of people, it was one of the biggest frustrations from the get-go.

Google issued multiple software patches attempting to tune recognition algorithms, but software can only do so much to compensate for mediocre optical hardware.

In my mind, the most damaging issue was cellular connectivity.

So instead of using Qualcomm’s class-leading modems, the Pixel 6 series tried out Samsung’s Exynos 5123 modem. You’ll know all about this if you use either phone for any extended period of time. Dropped calls, slow to send text messages, weak signal basically everywhere, even when in the visible range of a cell tower. It was a mess.

Even testing showed it was just bad compared to other flagship phones. It was a disaster, and this isn’t something you can ever fix with a software update.

The software patch debacle

Despite Android 12 being the biggest shift in the platform up until that point, and debuting on the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro, it was a very buggy update and one that needed near constant attention alongside the other issues this duo faced post-launch.

The situation spiraled after the disastrous December 2021 security update. The update introduced critical call-dropping bugs so severe that Google was forced to pull the release entirely and pause OTA rollouts for nearly a month while working on emergency fixes that pushed into late January 2022.

For a product line whose defining identity had always been pristine software and rapid, flawless monthly updates, the December-January release cycle was not a good look. That’s not discounting some early issues with the new and improved camera systems onboard.

Finally, modern camera hardware

For four straight generations prior, Google clung stubbornly to the aging 12.2-megapixel Sony IMX363 sensor. I’d say that the company was overrelying on computational photography wizardry to squeeze blood from a stone. With the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro, Google finally listened to the complaints and paired its legendary image pipeline with some actual cutting-edge optical hardware.

Both phones pack a 1/1.31-inch 50MP Samsung ISOCELL GN1 main sensor, which captures roughly 150% more light than the Pixel 5. The resulting images delivered that lovely natural optical shallow depth of field, stunning dynamic range, and rich textures that no longer relied on over-sharpening algorithms. Night Sight became noticeably faster, and skin tones were rendered with unprecedented fidelity thanks to the introduction of Real Tone tuning.

On the Pixel 6 Pro, Google added a dedicated 48MP 4x periscope telephoto lens. This transformed the Pro into a versatile long-range shooter, producing clean hybrid zoom up to 20x.

I guess like basically everything else on the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro, the transition to a larger physical sensor was not entirely smooth. Close-up shots frequently suffered from optical fringing and falloff around the edges of text documents, highlighting the lack of dedicated macro capabilities on the standard ultra-wide camera. Before updates, there was a ton of oversharpening that felt like a hangover from the previously 12MP main sensor era that had to be ironed out.

Video recording, while improved through HDRnet processing, still lagged behind the iPhone in low-light stability and frame consistency. Still, the Pixel 6 camera setup finally looked and shot like real flagship hardware.

How the Pixel 6 shaped future generations

In retrospect, the Pixel 6 was the messy blueprint that made everything that came after it possible. Google treated this generation as a clean break, and the hard lessons learned directly dictated the roadmap for subsequent flagships.

The industrial design was one of the strongest areas, and we’ve seen it refined into an integrated visor on the Pixel 7 and 8 series, eliminating the delicate glass visor seams and smoothing out corner transitions. The optical fingerprint reader, while still not top-tier ultrasonic until the Pixel 9 series, saw improved hardware revisions and accompanying software facial recognition fallback added to the next device.

On the connectivity front, the widespread backlash pushed Google to iteratively address modem efficiency and reception, moving through newer Samsung modems before laying the groundwork for better connectivity in recent years. The camera sensor’s higher baseline established on the 6 series provided the stable foundation for Google’s imaging algorithms to mature over several release cycles. The consistency is back and remains a strong suit of the latest phones once again.

	

Crucially, the aggressive $599 pricing of the base Pixel 6 in some ways reset consumer expectations across the industry. I don’t doubt that it proved premium hardware and custom silicon did not require a four-figure entry fee. A lot of that has been ditched in recent years, but the point remains.

The Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro were fundamentally flawed pioneers for Google. They were the firm’s most ambitious hardware undertaking to date, and simultaneously one of the most frustrating phone series to live with during their initial launch window and beyond.

If the Pixel 5 was a safe play ahead of this big pitch, the Pixel 6 was a risky dive into deep waters. It stumbled badly yet without those painful growing pains; the more polished, confident, and reliable Pixel devices we enjoy today simply would not exist.

title: Apple’s inventory surges 154% as memory chip costs climb
snippet: Apple says unprecedented memory chip costs will continue to rise, raising questions about future device prices as its inventory climbs to $14.5 billion.
fullText:
Apple’s stockpiling of inventory, particularly computer memory, continued in its fiscal fourth quarter, according to earnings reported Monday. The company reported that its inventory increased significantly in the quarter, growing from $11.09 billion in Q3 to $14.54 billion in Q4, a jump of 31.1%. Year-over-year, inventory grew 154.3% from $5.72 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Apple’s forecast of a 45% to 46% gross margin in the December quarter was largely attributed to the impact of higher memory costs. The company reported a gross margin of 47.9% for the September quarter.

“What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” said Apple CEO John Ternus, speaking to analysts on the call. “As we said earlier in the September quarter, we did see higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, which were partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on certain non-memory components.”

He said that the company expected “even higher memory costs” in the December quarter, which would be partially offset by price increases implemented earlier this year on some devices, including Mac and iPad at the end of June and iPhones in September.

Ternus also said that beyond December, Apple expects memory costs “continuing to increase.”

“As we said before, we do believe we’ll see a decreasing benefit from the carry-in inventory on memory over time,” he noted, adding that the company was increasing its purchases of this key component. “As we work to improve supply, our manufacturing purchase obligations have increased by 33 billion dollars from June to the September quarter, which you’ll see in our annual filing when it comes out tomorrow.” 

Apple also brought COO Sabih Khan, who oversees the company’s supply chain and manufacturing, onto the call to address questions about memory. He reiterated the increased purchase obligations but did not rule out future price increases on Apple devices.

The company also blamed supply constraints for weak iPad sales in the quarter. The iPad was one of the only product segments that didn’t grow, even as iPhone and Mac sales beat estimates. iPad revenue was $6.2 billion, below analysts’ expectations of $6.7 billion. The figure was also down 10% from the prior year.

title: Apple confirms iOS 27.3 beta is coming next week with Apple Intelligence in China
snippet: Apple today took the unusual step of confirming when its next iOS developer beta is expected to arrive, as part of an announcement detailing the upcoming launch of Apple Intelligence in China. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple today took the unusual step of confirming when its next iOS developer beta is expected to arrive, as part of an announcement detailing the upcoming launch of Apple Intelligence in China. Here are the details.

A bit of context

In mid-July, Reuters reported that, following a lengthy back-and-forth with Chinese regulators and multiple delays, Apple Intelligence had finally cleared a major regulatory hurdle ahead of its long-awaited launch in the country.

Then, a couple of weeks ago, Bloomberg reported that Apple was planning to launch Apple Intelligence in China in December as part of iOS 27.3, although without Siri AI and other newer features.

The following day, China’s state-backed media outlet The Paper reported that Tim Cook had confirmed regulatory approval for the platform, with a test version expected before the end of October.

Then, just last Monday, Apple released iOS 27.2 and its counterparts, expanding Siri AI support to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. On the same day, the company announced that four more languages, including Traditional Chinese, would be supported by the end of the year.

However, while that announcement confirmed additional language support for Siri AI, it offered no updates on the rollout of Apple Intelligence in China, where Siri AI itself will remain unavailable for the time being.

While Apple typically releases the first beta of its next software update shortly after the previous version becomes available, iOS 27.3 has yet to materialize.

Now, as spotted by MacRumors, a press release published on Apple’s Chinese Newsroom website confirms that testing of Apple Intelligence in China will begin on November 4, as part of the next iOS developer beta.

Importantly, Apple has only confirmed November 4 as the start of Apple Intelligence testing in China, not necessarily the release date of iOS 27.3 beta 1 itself.

Apple Intelligence coming to China

In the press release, Apple confirms that users in China will get an improved Siri experience, including Type to Siri and the ability to access Alibaba’s Qwen for certain requests, but not Siri AI itself.

The Qwen integration will also extend to Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence. According to Apple, users will be able to ask questions about photos and documents, including PDFs and presentations, as well as generate original content from scratch through Writing Tools. Users will be able to access Qwen by signing into their accounts or using Sign in with Apple.

Other features included in the initial rollout are Live Translation in Messages, FaceTime, and Phone, Writing Tools, Genmoji, Clean Up in Photos, natural-language photo searches, priority notifications, notification summaries, and Smart Reply, among others.

Apple also noted that the initial rollout will be exclusive to the iPhone, with support for other platforms coming only after the necessary regulatory approvals have been obtained.

The features will be available on the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max, iPhone 16 and later, iPhone Air, and iPhone Duo, with both Siri and the device language required to be set to either English or Simplified Chinese.

The company also confirmed that the features will become publicly available in December, with the official release of iOS 27.3.

title: Apple spent a record $45.77 billion on R&D in fiscal 2026, up 32%
snippet: Apple’s research and development expenses reached a new all-time high in fiscal 2026, climbing 32% year over year to $45.77 billion. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple’s research and development expenses reached a new all-time high in fiscal 2026, climbing 32% year over year to $45.77 billion. Here are the details.

Apple’s R&D spending reaches new record-high

While it may have taken Apple longer than some wished it had to ramp up R&D in the face of growing competition in AI, the company has significantly accelerated its spending over the past year.

As Apple shared in its Q4 2026 results, it spent $11.73 billion on R&D, bringing its total spending for fiscal 2026 to $45.77 billion, a 32% increase compared to the $34.55 billion it spent in fiscal 2025.

During an earnings call earlier this year, former CEO Tim Cook said Apple was “clearly investing more,” adding that R&D was “accelerating much higher than the company” overall. CFO Kevan Parekh also explained that AI-related spending was being added to the investments Apple was already making in its existing product roadmap.

Interestingly, today’s figures also suggest that Apple’s R&D spending may be starting to level off.

Note: Figures in the chart have been rounded to two decimal places, in billions of US dollars.

While Apple’s Q4 2026 R&D expenses were up 32% from $8.87 billion in the year-ago quarter, they were virtually unchanged from Q3, increasing by just $1 million. As the chart above shows, Apple’s R&D spending jumped significantly at the beginning of fiscal 2026, but has since stabilized at a much higher level than in previous years.

title: Strava adds Google Gemini integration with personalized workout insights
snippet: Strava expanded its AI integrations with Google Gemini this week, allowing subscribers to get personalized insights based on their workout history. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Strava expanded its AI integrations with Google Gemini this week, allowing subscribers to get personalized insights based on their workout history. Here are the details.

Strava expands AI integration to Gemini

A few months ago, fitness tracking platform Strava launched an integration with Claude using the Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing users to analyze their workout history and training performance through natural-language conversations with Anthropic’s AI assistant.

MCP is an open standard (created by Anthropic and later donated to the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation) that allows AI assistants to connect to external apps and services to access information and perform tasks on behalf of users.

This week, Strava announced an expansion of its AI integrations, bringing similar capabilities to Google Gemini.

As the company explained, Strava subscribers “who connect Strava directly to Gemini will get more contextual and personalized answers grounded in their activity history.” The company added that the integration is entirely optional and read-only

From the announcement:

Once connected, users can ask Gemini things such as:

“Am I getting faster at the same heart rate?” See what’s different in your volume, consistency, and mix of sports, without scrolling through months of activities.

“Can you give me a detailed analysis of how I performed in my last race?” Understand how your effort played out, mile by mile.

“How is my strength training impacting my running?”Synthesize trends across any sports you do on Strava.

And with our most recent update, users can also ask:

“What’s my fastest 10K this year vs. all time?” Compare your best efforts side by side, with the date and activity behind each, to see how far you’ve come and what’s still in reach. 

“How much did the heat slow me down on Saturday’s long run?” Work out whether it was your legs or the forecast. The temperature, humidity, wind, and conditions from your activity are now part of the picture.

“How long is my longest running streak on Strava?” Check your current and longest streaks, by sport, and when your current one started, so you know where you stand before the day is over. Or ask, “How long is my run streak?”

The rollout will be limited to the US at first, with the integration available to Strava subscribers regardless of their Gemini plan. Strava has not announced when it might expand to other countries.

title: John Ternus addresses iPhone Duo supply constraints, display issue
snippet: Today Apple reported record Q4 earnings, which beat Wall Street expectations overall. And in an interview with Reuters, CEO John Ternus addressed current iPhone Duo supply constraints and also referenced units that have been returned for display issues. more…
fullText:
Today Apple reported record Q4 earnings, which beat Wall Street expectations overall. And in an interview with Reuters, CEO John Ternus addressed current iPhone Duo supply constraints and also referenced units that have been returned for display issues.

Apple is ‘not able to predict’ when iPhone Duo will reach supply-demand balance, says Ternus

Apple’s latest quarterly earnings did not include any sales for the iPhone Duo. That’s because it covered a period running July-September, and the Duo didn’t go on sale until October.

But Wall Street is understandably still very curious about how sales for the foldable are going. Especially as relates to revenue forecasts for the current quarter.

In an interview with Reuters, Ternus addressed two aspects of the iPhone Duo: supply constraints and units that have had display issues.

Regarding supply, it sounds like Apple doesn’t know when it might reach supply-demand balance:

“Duo is constrained as of today,” Ternus said. “The ramp is going well, and we’re working hard to get it to as many customers as quickly as possible, but at this point, we’re not ‌able to ⁠predict when supply and demand will be in balance.”

Currently, shipping estimates from the Apple Store are still set for late January. That’s where they’ve stayed since the first pre-orders immediately sold out on October 16.

On the matter of iPhone Duo screens cracking, Ternus was brief and essentially repeated what Apple had previously confirmed: that the issue is real, but limited to a very small number of units.

Ternus told Reuters that “a very small percentage” of iPhone Duo units had been returned with display issues. Apple is replacing those units with new models.

title: Apple Wallet driver’s licenses coming to three new states soon
snippet: Apple Wallet driver’s licenses recently launched in Virginia and Oklahoma, but three more states are expected to follow soon, bringing us close to 20 US states on board. more…
fullText:
Apple Wallet driver’s licenses recently launched in Virginia and Oklahoma, but three more states are expected to follow soon, bringing us close to 20 US states on board.

Utah, Kentucky, and North Carolina appear set to launch driver’s licenses in Apple Wallet soon

Digital IDs are becoming far more common than they were when Apple first added support in the Wallet app back in 2021. And today, 16 US states plus Puerto Rico support the feature on iPhone.

The latest additions, Virginia and Oklahoma, debuted just in the last couple months.

And it looks like three more states will be coming soon:

Utah

Kentucky

North Carolina

This summer evidence was discovered of both Utah and Virginia being added to Apple’s backend for driver’s license support. Virginia has since gone live, so it’s expected that Utah will launch as one of the next supported states.

Kentucky previously announced it will support Apple Wallet driver’s licenses after upgrading its digital ID system this summer. All indications are that the upgrade has been completed, so based on the state’s original plans, we should see licenses in Apple Wallet soon.

North Carolina recently announced the launch of its new digital driver’s license system. As part of the announcement, it confirmed licenses will be supported in Apple Wallet by early 2027.

Additional states might always surprise us and launch in Wallet before Utah, Kentucky, or North Carolina. We’ve seen a clear acceleration of states signing on to offer Wallet driver’s licenses.

But for now at least, the three states above appear the strongest candidates to debut soon.

For more info on states that have pledged Apple Wallet support, see our coverage here.

title: Apple’s best MacBook Pro decision this week had nothing to do with touch
snippet: Apple’s new touchscreen MacBook Pro brings plenty of welcome upgrades, but one of the best things about this week’s launch is what the company decided not to change. more…
fullText:
Apple’s new touchscreen MacBook Pro brings plenty of welcome upgrades, but one of the best things about this week’s launch is what the company decided not to change.

Apple’s decision to keep the old Macs around feels like a welcome glitch in the system

Was I aching for a touchscreen Mac? Not particularly. But I can see how useful it might be for a great deal of users, and I’m happy that their day has finally come. Or will come, starting November 6.

But I’ve been aching for a new Mac. Though my 2023 M2 Pro 16-inch MacBook Pro is still a great machine, its 16GB of RAM is starting to feel a bit cramped. Past me knew this was a mistake.

With the prospect of a revamped MacBook Pro just around the corner, I spent the past few weeks excited about the possibility of biting the bullet and splurging for a new one, even though there had been very conflicting rumors about which chips it would pack.

Although in my heart of hearts I had acquiesced to the idea that the new touchscreen MacBook Pro would get the same chips as the current non-touchscreen line, I was also holding on to the hope that Apple would throw in some performance gains to sweeten the rumored $400 premium deal it would carry.

Right? Right?

Well, no.

Performance-wise, the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is identical to the non-touchscreen models, though there is a case to be made that its redesigned thermal system could make it run faster despite using the same chip, though the changes appear to be aimed more at keeping the display cool than improving heat dissipation. Time, and reviews, will tell.

Which makes Apple’s decision to keep the non-touchscreen M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pro for sale all that more welcome and unexpected.

Even when Apple introduced the Touch Bar back in 2016, the only non-Touch Bar option left was the entry-level 13-inch MacBook Pro. If you wanted a more powerful Mac or a 15-inch model, you had to get with the program and pony up the extra $300 for the 13-inch model with Touch Bar, or $400 for the redesigned 15-inch model.

Yes, there is plenty new with the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. Tandem OLED display, improved thermal performance, thinner, lighter design, slimmer bezels, redesigned audio system, Dynamic Island (debatable for some, I know), and even the return of the glowing Apple logo (woo!) on the lid are all welcome additions. Oh yeah, and “it has touch as well.”

Put all of that together, and the $400 premium is arguably not that unreasonable.

But if, like me, these improvements feel secondary to the performance boost you’re prioritizing for this particular upgrade, getting those same specs for effectively $400 less (or using those $400 for better specs!) feels like a pretty great deal for all parties involved, future me included.

Will future me have preferred that I wait for the M7 generation? Possibly. But then again, waiting for the perfect moment to upgrade is what got me into this situation in the first place, recent price hikes and all.

fullText:
Google has updated its Android distribution numbers with the latest update showing that Android 17 is on just 1% of devices, while Android 16 now makes up the biggest slice of the pie. 

Updated as of October 19, Google’s latest Android distribution numbers offer a peek into the rollout speed of Android 17. Having released to Pixel phones in June, the update has been available for roughly four months. 

At this point, though, Android 17 makes up just 1% of active Android devices, Google’s data shows.

That’s compared to over 25% for Android 16, which released last year. Android 16 was on 7.5% of devices in Google’s last update in December 2025/January 2026, which landed several months after Google released the update. The timing here requires context, as major players like Samsung have only started widely rolling out their Android 17 updates in the past few weeks and are very unlikely to be included in this 1%.

	

	

The growth of Android 16 is pretty impressive, too, as older versions tend to be still be more widely in use at this point in the schedule, but Android 16 has managed to consolidate quite a bit. 

Google dropped Android 5 (Lollipop) from its data with this update, with Android 5.1 making up just 0.2% of active devices. Android 11, for reasons unclear, still holds over 10%, while Android 12 has dropped to 9.6%. Android 11 has had a higher share in the past few updates.

title: Alphabet reports Q3 2026 revenue of $127.6 billion
snippet: Alphabet today announced Q3 2026 earnings with $127.6 billion in revenue. These numbers range from July to September. more…
fullText:
Alphabet today announced Q3 2026 earnings with $127.6 billion in revenue. These numbers range from July to September.

Revenue is up 25% from $102.3 billion in Q3 2025, with operating income at $40.58 billion and net income of $26.17 billion for this quarter (versus $34.9 billion a year ago). For comparison, Alphabet reported $119.8 billion in revenue and $112.1 billion in net income last quarter.

We had a strong quarter and are now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate. Our deep full stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with Alphabet revenues growing 25% year-over year.

Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-overyear query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years.

Google Cloud revenues grew 103%, powered by huge demand for our AI infrastructure and AI solutions. We’re also seeing strong demand for our TPU systems across a wide range of customers.

Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon are now leading at the frontier. Overall, our first-party model APIs are now processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times what we processed a year ago.

On top of that, the Gemini app has reached one billion users—making it the fastest-growing product in Google’s history—and we surpassed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally, including trials.

We’re excited by the range of big opportunities ahead of us.”

Sundar Pichai, CEO

In Q3 2026, YouTube ad revenue was $11.2 billion (versus $10.26 billion a year ago), while Cloud reported $30.71 billion (compared to $15.16 billion).

“Google subscriptions, platforms, and devices” — which includes hardware, Play Store, and non-advertising YouTube revenues — reported $14.29 billion, compared to $12.87 billion the same quarter last year.

	

“Other Bets” continues to lose money. It reported $372 million in revenue compared to $344 million in Q3 of 2025. It lost $2.04 billion compared to $1.4 billion in the same quarter of last year.

title: Google adding more Connected Apps to Gemini & Search with new dev platform
snippet: Google today announced the Connected Apps Platform as a “unified way for more app developers to bring their capabilities directly into Gemini and Search.” more…
fullText:
Google today announced the Connected Apps Platform as a “unified way for more app developers to bring their capabilities directly into Gemini and Search.”

Existing third-party Connected Apps let you access Adobe, Dropbox, Instacart, OpenTable, Ticketmaster, and other services — now numbering over 50 — from the Gemini app. Google also announced a new Calm integration that will be available in the coming weeks. These @-integrations join first-party offerings like Google Workspace, Photos, and YouTube. To date, the creation process has required working closely with Google. 

Google is now expanding availability on multiple fronts, starting with the Connected Apps Platform. It’s billed as a way to “build once and reach high-intent users.” Developers need to have a cloud-hosted MCP server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs. They then register, test, and submit their Connected Apps using the new Google Connected Console. This new website lets them track traffic, latency, and error rates, as well as control brand identity.

In addition to the Gemini app, Google will soon make existing Connected Apps available in Search. Developers can “choose whether [their app] will go live in Search, the Gemini app, or both.” As part of the recent redesign, the Gemini app gained a new Customize page.

	

Developers can sign up for the preview at developers.google.com/connected-apps. Google is opening up access in phases over the coming months.

title: Here’s what’s coming for the MacBook Pro next year, per report
snippet: Apple just unveiled a huge update to the Mac lineup last week, introducing the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. In a new report, Bloomberg has details on what’s next for the MacBook Pro, with multiple new models expected to come next year. more…
fullText:
Apple just unveiled a huge update to the Mac lineup last week, introducing the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display.

In a new report, Bloomberg has details on what’s next for the MacBook Pro, with multiple new models expected to come next year.

What’s coming to the MacBook Pro next year? 

Apple’s current MacBook Pro lineup features multiple different tiers:

M6 MacBook Pro

M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pro

M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display and Touch

In the latest edition of his Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman says Apple will introduce a new version of the base MacBook Pro powered by the M7 chip next year. This machine will adopt the same design as the new high-end MacBook Pros introduced last week, which are thinner, lighter, and have slimmer bezels.

	

The report also says Apple will introduce a second-generation touchscreen MacBook Pro next year, powered by M7 Pro and M7 Max chips.

Gurman previously reported on Apple’s plans to skip the M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, instead jumping all the way to the M7 family “as early as the first half of next year.” At the time, Gurman said the M7 line “is designed primarily around major advancements to on-device AI processing.”

Looking further into the future, Gurman eventually expects Apple to converge the MacBook Pro lineup:

With the first version, Apple is charging a $400 premium to add touch, OLED and the Dynamic Island interface. The M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros without touch are sticking around, but I’d be surprised if Apple continued developing non-touch versions of its high-end laptop models. There’s an added burden on its engineering, marketing and manufacturing teams to manage two sets of high-end MacBook Pros, and the prices are close enough for convergence to not be that far off.

What do you think of the current MacBook Pro lineup? Should Apple prioritize converging the touchscreen and non-touchscreen models? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Samsung can’t decide between a larger Galaxy Z Fold 9 or one with worse specs, and neither can I
snippet: Following a smash hit in the smaller and wider Galaxy Z Fold 8, Samsung is obviously weighing its options behind the scenes when it comes to sequels. According to one leaker, the company is currently deciding between adding another Galaxy Z Fold 9 with a larger display, or one with lesser specs, and I can’t decide which one I want to see either. more…
fullText:
Following a smash hit in the smaller and wider Galaxy Z Fold 8, Samsung is obviously weighing its options behind the scenes when it comes to sequels. According to one leaker, the company is currently deciding between adding another Galaxy Z Fold 9 with a larger display, or one with lesser specs, and I can’t decide which one I want to see either.

Leaker Lanzuk on Naver says that Samsung is adding more options to the Galaxy Z Fold 9 lineup next year after the Galaxy Z Fold 8 garnered “much better response than expected” (translated). It’s all-but-official that Samsung is expanding the lineup – we’ve heard this repeatedly at this point – but exactly what joins the lineup remains unclear.

This latest rumor suggests two possibilities. 

The first is a larger version of the Galaxy Z Fold 8, a “Galaxy Z Fold 9 Plus,” the leaker suggests. This wouldn’t be an Ultra device, but rather would share the same wide form factor as the standard Fold 9, just with a larger pair of displays.

	

The other option is a “Galaxy Z Fold 9 FE” which would downgrade the specs to achieve a lower price point. Samsung tried this with the Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE to essentially no success, but the company’s cuts on that device were far from compelling on a form factor that was already in decline.

Samsung is said to be testing both form factors and “a decision will be made soon,” but only one of the two would move to production and a full release. 

9to5Google’s Take

Personally, I’m split here. I’ve been using the Galaxy Z Fold 8 as my daily smartphone since its launch, and the size is certainly one of its most attractive features. On the one hand, I’d love to have a larger version for better media consumption and multitasking, but I also think Samsung would run into diminishing returns with a larger size. The wider form factor wouldn’t scale nicely to a larger size too, I think.

Meanwhile, a more affordable version seems like a clear win. This form factor has so clearly resonated with customers, and having an option that makes strategic cuts to hit a price of say, $1,400, would be a home run. However, given Samsung’s existing struggles with profitability amid RAMageddon and ever-rising prices, that also feels unrealistic.

I’m very torn on which would be the better option. Which one would you prefer?

title: Apple and OpenAI trade secrets lawsuit now has an official trial date
snippet: Judge Edward Davila today formally established the schedule for Apple’s trade secrets misappropriation lawsuit against two former employees, OpenAI, and io Products, including a trial date. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Judge Edward Davila today formally established the schedule for Apple’s trade secrets misappropriation lawsuit against two former employees, OpenAI, and io Products, including a trial date. Here are the details.

Apple and OpenAI set for July 2027 trial

A couple of weeks ago, during an October 14 case management conference, Judge Edward Davila instructed Apple and the defendants to agree on a proposed schedule for the lawsuit, working toward a tentative trial date of July 19, 2027.

The parties were given until October 23 to submit their proposed schedule, which the judge has now formally established.

As we’ve been covering since July, Apple filed this lawsuit accusing the defendants of improperly accessing or using confidential information about its products and technologies to help advance OpenAI’s consumer hardware development efforts.

In recent days, Apple scored two procedural wins in its efforts to obtain expedited discovery, with Judge Davila granting the company access to additional documents and information from the defendants ahead of the normal discovery process.

In a case management order issued today, Davila established July 19, 2027, at 9 a.m. as the official trial date, with additional deadlines for discovery, motions, and pretrial proceedings in the meantime.

title: X for iPhone and iPad just added over a dozen new app icon options
snippet: Since X was called Twitter, the iPhone and iPad app has supported changing the default app icon to something with a bit more flair. Today’s app update overhauls the alternative icon set with more than a dozen new options. more…
fullText:
Since X was called Twitter, the iPhone and iPad app has supported changing the default app icon to something with a bit more flair. Today’s app update overhauls the alternative icon set with more than a dozen new options.

These are the first new icons to really arrive since X was renamed a few years ago.

The alt icon set was originally part of Twitter Blue, now called X Premium, which gives subscribers access to the icon choices. Twitter Blue briefly included seasonal icons.

	

Eventually, the Twitter logo was replaced with the X symbol, a few space options were thrown in, and the default became the black icon.

Today’s app update replaces the existing icons with all-new options, including more ground-level space options and more. 

Here’s the set included in today’s app release:

The new options are found within the X app on iPhone and iPad under Settings > Subscription > App Icons. Which is your favorite?

title: AAWireless expands beyond Android Auto adapters with new cooled Qi2 car charger
snippet: AAWireless is known for helping you convert a wired Android Auto connection into a wireless one, but the company is now launching a new product – an active-cooled Qi2 car charger. more…
fullText:
AAWireless is known for helping you convert a wired Android Auto connection into a wireless one, but the company is now launching a new product – an active-cooled Qi2 car charger.

“AAWireless Charge” is a Qi2 25W wireless car charger that costs $50. The charger is compatible with MagSafe, Pixelsnap, and Qi2 in general, and supports up to 25W charging speeds on compatible phones. 

“Charge” also includes active cooling support with a built-in fan that the company says is “quiet” when active. 

Included in the box you’ll find both an air vent mount as well as an adhesive base. There are also two magnetic ring adapters in the box for “Qi2 Ready” phones that don’t have magnets built-in or a magnetic case available. AAWireless says to use your car’s 12V outlet with the included adapter for “best performance,” but you can also use existing USB-C connections so long as they deliver enough power.

	

To be clear, there’s no wireless adapter built into the charger (as cool as that would be), but you can use this alongside an AAWireless adapter while driving, the company specifically mentions.

While AAWireless adapters remain available on Amazon, “AAWireless Charge” is available solely from the company’s website.

title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon with ‘significant gains across coding and agentic tasks’
snippet: Following the launch of Argon two weeks ago, Google today announced Gemini 4 Carbon as its next frontier model. more…
fullText:
Following the launch of Argon two weeks ago, Google today announced Gemini 4 Carbon as its next frontier model.

There are “significant gains” in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity defense (finding vulnerabilities). Notably, “Carbon ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59.”

Related: Google adding more Connected Apps to Gemini & Search with new dev platform

Google says this fast release is due to its researchers and models “working hand in hand to advance capabilities faster.”

Based on user feedback following the last launch, Google worked to improve Carbon across “coding, agentic, and scientific tasks, as well as full-stack web development and multimodal understanding.”

	

“With improved quality of output and artifacts in web development, Carbon jumps +89 elo points to land at #4 (1769) on WebDev Arena.”

For cybersecurity: 

“firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching.”

“On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates.”

On the safety front, Google worked to improve alignment and trained Carbon to “respond to complex or high-pressure tasks in the right way.”

Greater transparency and honesty: In our internal testing, Carbon cuts unsupported claims by approximately 2x over Argon. It puts methodological caveats directly into the deliverable or withholds blocked actions with a clear list of what remains required, rather than fabricating or hedging around missing evidence.

Improved collaboration with the user in the face of ambiguity: Rather than guessing or forcing a path forward, Carbon retrieves the relevant sources and surfaces discrepancies to the user before acting — as a result, users should observe a much better collaborative experience with Carbon.

Following through without overstepping: Carbon simultaneously reduced overreach by 26% and under-service by 29% resulting in much more reliable execution of multi-step plans end-to-end while respecting project constraints and staying strictly within scope.

Officially, Gemini 4 Carbon is “coming soon to developers, businesses, and consumers.” The model will first be available to “cyber defenders” this week.

Once available, Google will offer introductory pricing of “$2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off input token price.” Afterward, it will cost $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens.

title: Samsung launches a virtual cash back card for Wallet, completely unrelated to the Galaxy Card
snippet: Samsung announced a new way to earn and pay in Samsung Wallet using a new “Cash Card.” more…
fullText:
Samsung announced a new way to earn and pay in Samsung Wallet using a new “Cash Card.”

Not to be confused with the Galaxy Card credit card Samsung announced earlier this year, Cash Card is a new virtual account that reflects earned cash back through select purchases. Samsung says it’s partnering with Rakuten to let users find deals both online and in-store using a “Nearby” feature in Samsung Wallet on any Galaxy phone.

Since the app ties into Raktuen’s network, that catalog of deals is constantly updated and available to Samsung Wallet users. Samsung says that it includes over 3,500 brands and more than 25,000 in-store and dining options. New users will reportedly earn 10% cash back, with rates fluctuating throughout the year.

Anything earned gets added to the Samsung Cash Card, which appears in Samsung Wallet as another virtual card. Whatever balance you have can be used online or in-store. Users will be able to send money to and from other Samsung Wallet accounts. The press release says even tapping another Galaxy or Android device will initiate an instant transfer, with some safety guardrails, of course.

	

The Cash Card is simply another payment method for Galaxy users with Samsung’s branding on it. While it’s entirely unrelated, it’s interesting to hear of another card launch within the same few months as the Galaxy Card, which is Samsung’s new Visa credit card via a partnership with Barclays.

It’s also not the first cash back program for Samsung Wallet. One was added in 2018, though this new release seems to be a revamp with new partners.

The virtual Samsung Cash Card and new Rakuten deals are rolling out now in the US.

title: Russia now requires Apple to store user communications and hand them over if requested
snippet: As Bloomberg reported today, Apple and Microsoft are now subject to Russian regulations requiring companies to store users’ communications and provide them to security agencies if requested. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
As Bloomberg reported today, Apple and Microsoft are now subject to Russian regulations requiring companies to store users’ communications and provide them to security agencies if requested. Here are the details.

Apple now part of Russia’s surveillance registry

Apple and Microsoft are now in Russia’s state surveillance registry, joining companies and services such as Google Meet, WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, Cloudflare, and Blizzard Entertainment, all of which are required to store users’ messages, audio and video communications, and provide them to Russian security agencies if requested.

According to Bloomberg, Apple and Microsoft were added on October 2 to the “organizers of information dissemination” registry, which is maintained by Russia’s communications regulator, Roskomnadzor.

Here’s Bloomberg:

Companies on the list are required under Russian law to store local users’ correspondence, audio and video messages and turn that data over to security services if asked. They must also store in Russia information about users and the transmission of their communications for three years.

Companies that fail to comply can face fines and ultimately have access to their services restricted in Russia. Google and its Google Meet video-calling service were added to the same registry in January.

The move comes as Russia continues to tighten restrictions on foreign messaging services, having already blocked or limited access to platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, and Apple’s FaceTime.

Specific to Apple, the company’s relationship with Russia has become increasingly complicated since the country invaded Ukraine in 2022, prompting Apple to suspend product sales and exports while limiting services such as Apple Pay.

However, Apple continued operating the App Store in Russia, which has led to several disputes with local authorities.

In April, Russian users lost the ability to make new App Store purchases or renew subscriptions without an existing Apple Account balance, following government-imposed payment restrictions.

	

In June, the Kremlin demanded an explanation after Apple removed several apps developed by Russian state-controlled company VK from the App Store. Around the same time, Apple also removed banking apps linked to sanctioned Russian financial institutions.

More recently, in August, Russia’s antitrust regulator opened formal proceedings against Apple over its failure to preinstall the state-backed MAX messaging app and the RuStore app marketplace on its devices.

All of that said, neither Apple nor Microsoft has publicly commented on its inclusion in the registry or indicated whether it intends to comply with the requirements.

title: Reddit will soon require an account for most content
snippet: Earlier today Reddit announced that it’s rolling out social media-style ‘For You’ feeds, but that wasn’t the only big news today. Reddit also now says that it’s going to start requiring a logged-in account for accessing most of its content. more…
fullText:
Earlier today Reddit announced that it’s rolling out social media-style ‘For You’ feeds, but that wasn’t the only big news today. Reddit also now says that it’s going to start requiring a logged-in account for accessing most of its content.

Reddit transitioning to being primarily a service for logged-in users

Sara Fischer writes at Axios:

Reddit on Thursday said it’s moving to become a primarily logged-in experience, marking one of the most significant shifts in its 21-year history.

Reddit has long championed the open web. Now, it’s pushing to build a more direct relationship with users while also protecting its data from increased scraping in the AI era.

Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman said in an interview that the change is being made to “improve its user experience, bolster its ads business and prevent bots from scraping its proprietary data.”

	

The plan is to start testing the new logged-in experience this quarter, but only outside the US to start. It will then roll it out more broadly around the world.

What will Reddit users without an account be able to access? Huffman acknowledges they’re still finalizing those details. Per Axios though, the Reddit homepage will still be accessible to everyone. And if you visit the site “via search engines or shared links,” you’ll still be able to access the content.

However, if you try to browse Reddit in any other way or visit a specific subreddit without being logged in, it sounds like that will no longer be possible.

title: XREAL Aura is coming in November with a special $200-off launch discount
snippet: The first Android XR-powered smart glasses are almost here, and early adopters actually get a rare discount on the cutting-edge XREAL Aura hardware. more…
fullText:
The first Android XR-powered smart glasses are almost here, and early adopters actually get a rare discount on the cutting-edge XREAL Aura hardware.

XREAL Aura is set to redefine what a “VR headset” can be by combining the form factor of XREAL display glasses with a small compute puck that clips to your waistband. XREAL and Google have teased Project Aura for months, announcing the official name and price last month, and now XREAL just unveiled the special launch price and release date on stage at Google’s Android Developer Summit.

The special glasses launch in mid-November, with preorders starting today, October 28, at Xreal.com and Best Buy. XREAL Aura will initially be available in the United States, Canada, Japan, and South Korea (with a broader rollout in 2027) and is coming in two SKUs:

XREAL AURA 12GB + 256GB: $1,279, limited-time offer of $1,099 through December 2026

XREAL AURA 16GB + 512GB: $1,499, limited-time offer of $1,299 through December 2026

Both SKUs are available in standard and large sizes and come with an included carrying case that houses the glasses, compute puck, and cable. The cable is user-replaceable and uses a standard USB-C connection for longevity.

	

XREAL Aura will be launching alongside 150 made-for-XR experiences designed to showcase the power and capability of the new form factor. I got to use a near-final unit last month and was incredibly impressed with how XREAL and Google have been able to pull together the full Android XR experience on a pair of smart glasses, including full 6DoF spatial tracking and support for hand tracking and controllers.

XREAL Aura attaches via a USB-C cable to a compute puck, which is roughly the size of a phone. This has a generously sized trackpad on the front and a detachable belt clip on the back. The battery and Snapdragon Reality Elite chipset are inside the puck, taking the glasses’ weight down to just 95g (compared to ~500g for a VR headset). 

XREAL Aura specs

Weight

95g

Display

Sony micro-OLED, 1200p, 120Hz

Display comfort

TÜV Rheinland certified 5-star: High Visibility, Low Blue Light, Flicker Free, and Color Accuracy

Lenses

Prism lenses, 70-degree FoV, adjustable electrochromic dimming

Audio

Built-in Bose speakers, Bluetooth

Chipset

Snapdragon Reality Elite, Xreal X1S chip

Connectivity

USB-C, Wi-Fi

Inputs

Voice, hand, keyboard, trackpad, game controller

XREAL and GameSir have partnered to deliver a new game controller built specifically for XREAL Aura (and Android XR). This one sports a prominent Gemini button that gives immediate access to Gemini’s helpful gaming capabilities (it’s actually more helpful than you might initially imagine). I also used this controller last month and found it to be wonderful. It feels similar to an Xbox Elite controller, but it is not spatially tracked.

A wireless portable keyboard is also on the way for productivity and multi-window workflows, but you can use any mouse and keyboard you’d like with Aura. XREAL Aura also supports wired mirroring, so you can plug your laptop or gaming console directly into the compute puck and add a spatially-tracked window to your view.

Preorders are open now and, of course, you’ll save $200 if you order XREAL Aura before the end of the year.

title: Bambu’s nine-nozzle H3C foretells the future of 3D printing
snippet: The Bambu H3C. | Image: Bambu Lab Three years ago, I told you how home 3D printers had evolved for speed, producing parts in minutes that used to take hours or days. Now, the next evolution is here: printers that can swap between materials on the fly, mix different colors to produce nearly the full rainbow, mix soft and hard materials, and even mix different sizes of nozzle and different diameters of filament so you can switch between high speed and fine detail in a single print. Today, Bambu Lab is announcing its most advanced 3D printer yet, the $2,499 H3C, which can do all of that mixing goodness - by loading nine different rolls of filament into nine different print hea … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Three years ago, I told you how home 3D printers had evolved for speed, producing parts in minutes that used to take hours or days. Now, the next evolution is here: printers that can swap between materials on the fly, mix different colors to produce nearly the full rainbow, mix soft and hard materials, and even mix different sizes of nozzle and different diameters of filament so you can switch between high speed and fine detail in a single print.

Today, Bambu Lab is announcing its most advanced 3D printer yet, the $2,499 H3C, which can do all of that mixing goodness — by loading nine different rolls of filament into nine different print heads.

Even if you’d never buy a printer this pricy, even if you’ve sworn off Bambu printers for good, the H3C is the perfect vehicle for me to explain where the state of the art in home printing tech is headed.

While the H3C still only prints in one material at any given moment, Bambu’s new “Swaptek” system lets the printer swap in any of the eight other nozzles in six seconds flat. All nine tools are stored in a rack at the front of the printer, where they can independently preheat to the correct temperature right before they’re needed.

With Bambu’s new “PLA Palette” cyan, magenta, yellow, and white filament, I printed a beautiful rainbow bird feather that emulated most of the other colors between those inks. With a mix of flexible TPU and rigid PLA filaments, I was able to print a hard wristwatch housing with an integrated flexible watchband. With an ultra-soft “75A” TPU filament plus a harder 90A variety, I printed a breathable, wearable shoe that… didn’t quite fit, unfortunately. (I’ll measure and try again.)

To be clear, Bambu didn’t invent toolchanger printers or color mixing. You could even argue Bambu’s slightly behind the curve, particularly after the $700-$900 Snapmaker U1 and its four-color, five-second swaps pleasantly surprised the community earlier this year. (Prusa also sells its hotly anticipated 8-tool INDX system for $2,249, though I’ve heard it has some issues.)

But I would have never bought previous toolchangers for myself, because they don’t have a place to keep your filament dry when you’re not printing. (Wet filament is one of the biggest remaining causes of print failures.) The H3C theoretically changes that by storing its nine rolls in an ostensibly airtight auto-loading container called the AMS 3H. Two of those nine slots even have built-in dryers that can hit 85 degrees Celsius and keep on drying your filament while you print, a big step up from Bambu’s previous AMS systems.

I haven’t tried the H3C for long enough to tell you if it’s ready to buy, and I’ve definitely run into some quirks in my first couple weeks of testing. I’ve had to start every single print twice because the printer complains that its “toolhead camera” isn’t initializing properly, I once lost half a day of printing to a false-positive print failure detection, and the beta build of Bambu Studio provided to reviewers initially got confused when I tried to mix colors. (I’m told that last one will be fixed by launch, and Bambu eventually provided some troubleshooting steps for the toolhead camera close to embargo time.)

You also have to load flexible TPU filaments into the H3C manually, and I learned the hard way that not all of the printer’s nine slots can actually accept a roll of TPU without causing trouble. Slot #6 can load standard filaments, but if you load the flexible stuff, another printhead can snag it and cause a nasty jam:

This also isn’t a printer where you can quickly repair a nozzle without tools, or use previous-gen toolless H, P, and A series swappable nozzles. It’s an all-new system that involves some minor disassembly, and I’m not sure about Bambu’s decision to leave filament in the toolheads between prints where it might attract moisture.

Photo by Sean Hollister / The Verge

But so far, this seems like an easier, more reliable printer than the two-nozzle Bambu H2D was at launch. Other than the Slot #6 TPU jam, which Bambu actually warns reviewers about in a section of the reviewer’s guide that I missed reading, everything I’ve tried to print has come out great so far — and without creating a mountain of little “printer poop” waste when I switch between colors! Dramatically reduced waste is one of the benefits of having extra nozzles.

With any luck, the future of 3D printing won’t just be for hobbyists willing to figure out which colors of filament they need to order before each and every project, or obsessives who store dozens of colors in vacuum-sealed bags. Instead, it should be more like today’s inkjet printers — an entire rainbow of color, ready to go at a moment’s notice. And hopefully without all the inkjet printer shenanigans, of course.

If you like Bambu’s toolchanger system, you probably won’t have to pay $2,499 for long. Certification filing leaks show that the company’s already prepping a smaller “P3C” with seven tools and seven rolls of filament storage instead of nine.

Additionally, Bambu will let all three of its existing dual-nozzle printers print with two different sizes of nozzle by next spring, including the H2D, the H2C, and the X2D.

Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

Sean Hollister
excerpt:
Three years ago, I told you how home 3D printers had evolved for speed, producing parts in minutes that used to take hours or days. Now, the next evolution is here: printers that can swap between materials on the fly, mix different colors to produce nearly the full rainbow, mix soft and hard materials, and even mix different sizes of nozzle and different diameters of filament so you can switch between high speed and fine detail in a single print.

Today, Bambu Lab is announcing its most advanced 3D printer yet, the $2,499 H3C, which can do all of that mixing goodness — by loading nine different rolls of filament into nine different print heads.

title: iOS 27.2 adds new Find My feature at just the right time
snippet: iOS 27.2 is here, and alongside new features for Apple Photos, Messages, and Siri AI, the update also has a welcome addition for Find My: support for Apple TV 4K remotes. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 is here, and alongside new features for Apple Photos, Messages, and Siri AI, the update also has a welcome addition for Find My: support for Apple TV 4K remotes.

Siri Remote for Apple TV 4K now included in Find My app with iOS 27.2

Find My has long been the iPhone’s go-to hub for locating people as well as your Apple devices.

Except until now, there’s been one Apple device not included in the app.

The Siri Remote for Apple TV 4K has historically been absent from Find My. There was another way to locate it using the Remote app via Control Center, but most users probably didn’t realize that feature existed.

But with iOS 27.2, Apple TV remotes have now been added to the Find My app for location tracking. Open Find My in iOS 27.2 and go to the Devices tab, and compatible Siri Remotes (2nd gen and later) will now appear there.

It’s nice that Apple finally addressed this oversight, but the timing is no coincidence. That’s because the new Siri Remote (4th gen) is going to make finding a lost remote way easier.

	

The new remote features Precision Finding support and a built-in speaker. So the next time it’s lost somewhere in your house, your iPhone can direct you step-by-step to its location and trigger a noise to help.

The new Siri Remote is included with the 4th generation Apple TV 4K. But you can also buy it separately for $59 and get the same new features. 

The upgraded remote is compatible with all Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD models. To benefit from Precision Finding though, you’ll need an iPhone 17 or newer.

Did you know the Remote app offered support for finding a lost remote? Will you use the new feature in Find My? Let us know in the comments.

fullText:
Apple just released its earnings report for the fourth fiscal quarter of 2026. The company reported $114.5 billion in revenue, and $30.71 billion in net profit. Here’s the full breakdown.

Apple sees Q4 revenue climb 12% year over year

Last year, for its fourth fiscal quarter, Apple reported $102.47 billion in revenue, $27.47 billion in net profit, and earnings per share of $1.85. For this quarter, the company expected revenue to grow between 9% and 11% year over year, implying revenue of roughly $111.69 billion and $113.74 billion.

Apple has now released its Q4 2026 results, reporting:

Total revenue: $114.48 billion

Net profit: $30.71 billion

Earnings per share: $2.10

iPhone revenue: $57.58 billion

Mac revenue: $10.79 billion

iPad revenue: $6.23 billion

Wearables, Home, and Accessories revenue: $8.30 billion

Services revenue: $31.57 billion

Here’s Apple CEO John Ternus on today’s results:

“Today, Apple is proud to report a September quarter revenue record of $114.5 billion, up 12 percent from a year ago, with iPhone reaching a September quarter record and Services reaching an all-time high, capping off our best fiscal year ever. […] We’re closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet. That includes the iPhone Duo, the most transformational iPhone since the original, alongside iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, our most powerful iPhones yet. We also just introduced a whole new generation of hardware for the home and brought Touch to Mac for the first time. Together with the all-new Siri AI, it’s an incredible lineup to carry us into the holiday season.”

Apple CFO Kevan Parekh added:

“Apple delivered September quarter records for net income and EPS. Our record September quarter capped off a strong fiscal 2026, with all-time record revenue of $479 billion and double-digit EPS growth. […] We generated $28 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, allowing us to return $28 billion to shareholders. Thanks to our very high levels of customer satisfaction and loyalty, our installed base of active devices reached a new all-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments.”

title: Here’s how the new MacBook Pro and macOS 27 are optimized for touch
snippet: Apple just unveiled the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR, its first MacBook with a touch display. While Apple already added a handful of touch optimizations to macOS 27 Golden Gate earlier this year, there’s also a number of new optimizations that were unveiled alongside the new MacBook Pro. Here’s what Apple worked on. more…
fullText:
Apple just unveiled the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR, its first MacBook with a touch display. While Apple already added a handful of touch optimizations to macOS 27 Golden Gate earlier this year, there’s also a number of new optimizations that were unveiled alongside the new MacBook Pro. Here’s what Apple worked on.

Enlarged traffic light icons

With the new touchscreen MacBook Pro, the traffic light icons in the top left of an app window will get bigger when you’re tapping them, making the touch targets a little bit larger.

Image Credit: Max Weinbach

On screen gestures

Gestures that you can normally perform on the trackpad can also be performed on the screen. Whether that be a three-finger swipe up for mission control, three-finger swipes to switch spaces, pinching to zoom, or scrolling on a web page. You can also access Spotlight from the Dynamic Island, similar to how iPhones handle it on iOS 27.

iOS simulator

If you’re an app developer, you’ll really appreciate this change: with the new MacBook Pro, you can fully navigate the iOS simulator with touch. No need to try to replicate touch gestures on a trackpad.

When you interact with a context menu in the menu bar, each of the items within a menu will get a little bit larger for touch. Additionally, most optimized apps will have larger touch targets, even if the buttons don’t necessarily appear bigger.

Wrap up

All in all, there’s a handful of optimizations already in macOS 27 Golden Gate for the touchscreen MacBook Pro. On top of what was named here, Apple also added pull to refresh in Safari and slightly larger spacing between menu bar items to all Macs with macOS 27.

	

Apple also says there’s more to come on the Mac when it comes to touch optimizations, so we’ll likely see much more in store at the next WWDC.

title: AMVR’s new head strap is my favorite way to keep cool with a Meta Quest 3 or 3S
snippet: The upgraded AMVR BS1 head strap includes better ergonomics, a built-in fan, magnetic rechargeable batteries, and a new breathable mesh top support for ultimate comfort. more…
fullText:
The upgraded AMVR BS1 head strap includes better ergonomics, a built-in fan, magnetic rechargeable batteries, and a new breathable mesh top support for ultimate comfort.

I don’t know how companies like AMVR and BoboVR keep doing it, but AMVR’s latest head strap is now the most comfortable cooling head strap I’ve ever used for the Meta Quest 3 and Quest 3S. If you’re still using the included cloth head strap or haven’t used a “cooling head strap” before, here’s how it works.

The AMVR BS1 uses a breathable forehead pad attached via magnets to the support bar. Inside that support bar is an adjustable-speed fan, which you can easily adjust using the recessed wheel on the right side of the head strap. This fan keeps sweat down and helps prevent lens fog, two problems that can be a constant annoyance.

The fan is powered by the magnetically detachable, rechargeable 8,800mAh battery pack that mounts on the back of the head strap, helping to even out the weight distribution across the headset. That battery pack will also charge your Quest while playing and adds around 4 hours of additional play time. You can always purchase more packs to keep things going for longer, if you need to.

	

AMVR BS1 at Amazon (10% off)

Lots of padding can be found all around the headset, and the mesh support on top accepts any weight that remains. Every bit of padding is easily removable and washable, so you can keep things clean and tidy (especially if you share your headset with others). You can also get extra pads if you’d rather do it that way.

The back of the head strap cradles your skull with a mix of half supple padding and half grippy silicone. You’ll be double happy there, as the pad on the top part further cushions any headset weight, while the silicone keeps the headset from slipping forward and shifting weight onto your cheeks.

If you don’t need a fan, the BoboVR M3 Pro+ is currently $17 less than the AMVR BS1. I find the BoboVR M3 Pro+’s hybrid design to be slightly more comfortable, but the lack of a fan is a big negative for this particular BoboVR strap.

Once you’ve chosen a head strap, grab an AMVR FC4M face pad to add another layer of comfort to the headset. Like the AMVR BS1’s forehead pad, this face pad attaches to the Quest 3 (NOT the Quest 3S) via magnets and is made of breathable, easy-to-clean material. It’s perfect for staying cool year-round and makes the Quest so, so much more comfortable.

title: Gemini 4 Carbon lags just behind Claude in benchmark, but wins in value
snippet: Google’s new frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, brings some welcome improvements and while it doesn’t top the charts in a new benchmark, it does provide much more bang for your buck. more…
fullText:
Google’s new frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, brings some welcome improvements and while it doesn’t top the charts in a new benchmark, it does provide much more bang for your buck. 

SemiAnalysis, an AI research and analysis firm, recently published its new frontier-level benchmark, GDPx which includes numbers for Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon model. The leaderboard includes every major frontier model from the likes of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta and details both the score and cost for each model.

The benchmark includes 206 tasks across finance, materials science, cybersecurity, software engineering, legal, biology, and several other domains (topics). 

Topping the results is Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5, but Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon is very close behind. The difference between the two is relatively minimal, but the cost is the biggest factor to consider here. Where Claude’s cost came out to around $51 per task, Gemini was just over $16 per task. Gemini also beat the next model on the list, GPT-6 Astra, which scored lower while costing more than both at about $54 per task.

	

The report notes that taking out cybersecurity, biology, and alignment domains shuffles the results. Safety guardrails in Claude and GPT models puts GPT-6 Astra at the top of the list with GPT 6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 outranking Gemini 4 Carbon. SemiAnalysis says that this better aligns with their “subjective impressions” of each model. 

As for Google’s existing frontier model, Gemini 4 Argon, it ranks in eighth place on both lists, beating Meta’s Muse Wonder, but below Wonder Full. Argon’s costs in this particular benchmark are only slightly lower than Carbon.

Both of Google’s models score better than OpenAI and Anthropic models when focused on cybersecurity, but do fall behind Meta’s Muse models, which the benchmark found to be the best “by a meaningful margin.”

Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28 and touted “significant gains,” but the public release date has not been confirmed just yet. It is “coming soon” for most customers. Google’s own benchmark, below, beat GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5 in many aspects.

title: GTA 6 Sneakers: Rockstar Games, Nike and Travis Scott Reportedly Team Up
snippet: You could see these shoes the same day Rockstar releases the long-awaited game.
fullText:
Rockstar Games is releasing the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 in just a few weeks, on Nov. 19, and rapper Travis Scott and Nike are reportedly getting in on the game’s hype. According to Sneaker News, Nike, Rockstar Games and Travis Scott are working together to release a set of Nike Air Force 1 ’07 sneakers themed around the upcoming game. Reports suggest the shoes will retail for $130 and be available on Nov. 19, the same day as the game’s release.

The shoes will reportedly be available in three colorways. Those palettes are supposedly “White/White/Fire Pink,” “Black/Black/Fire Pink” and “Multicolor/Pale Ivory/Black/Bold Berry/Fire Pink.” The sneaker account prm.stocks.01 shared images of what the black pair would look like if you want to take a peek.

The shoe will reportedly have the reverse swoosh logo traditionally seen on other Travis Scott sneakers, and the leather appears to feature a grid that looks like city blocks.

			

More from CNET

The shoes have six stars on the heels, the report says, a nod to the six-star wanted level, which makes its return to the Grand Theft Auto series in the upcoming game. Grand Theft Auto 5 replaced the six-star system with a five-star system.

The sneakers will also supposedly come with a $100 GTA-branded money band around the shoe’s toe box. Other Nike shoes, like the different colors of the Concepts x Nike SB Dunk Low Lobsters, have had removable rubber bands, too.

And the shoe’s midsole reportedly replaces the “AIR” lettering normally on all Air Force One models with the letters “GTA.” There are likely more details that reference the game hidden throughout the shoe.

Neither Nike nor Rockstar Games immediately responded to my request for comment.

While there will reportedly be three colors of this shoe available, I think Nike, Rockstar and Travis Scott could have stopped at the black pair. I’m sure the other two colorways are fine, but it’s a joke that black Air Force 1 sneakers are used in various criminal and illegal activities, making that pair a perfect representation of the Grand Theft Auto series.

I appreciate the six-star and money band details we see in the photos, and the pink gives the pairs a nice hint of Vice City-coded color without being too much. The black pair of these shoes reportedly comes with black and pink laces, and I’d lace up the pink ones if I ever got these shoes.

However, since these are a collab between Nike, Rockstar and Travis Scott, I’m not expecting to see them on my feet. Travis Scott and Nike collaborations usually release in limited quantities, so it’s difficult to get a pair. You could always buy the shoes on eBay, StockX or a similar marketplace, but some Travis Scott and Nike collabs sell on the aftermarket for more than $1,000, depending on your size. And I’m not spending that much on a single pair of shoes. I’ve got a mortgage to pay, thank you very much.

title: T-Mobile Adds 5 Gig Plan to Its Fiber Home Internet Lineup
snippet: The carrier has added a top-tier home internet option for households hitting bandwidth limits.
fullText:
Is your home internet fast enough? That’s a trick question, because who doesn’t want faster internet? The real question is, how much are you willing to pay for more speed?

T-Mobile’s answer is $90 a month for its new Fiber 5 Gig service, which includes a 10-year price guarantee for the premium plan. (That amount is based on AutoPay billing, with taxes and fees added on top.)

Kicking off Nov. 3, the Fiber 5 Gig plan includes equal download and upload speeds, unlimited data and a mesh Wi-Fi extender, if requested, to help spread the signal throughout a household.
